environment.description: Same FastAPI service deployed behind AWS API Gateway (HTTP API type) with a Lambda authorizer that performs request integrity verification. The Lambda authorizer extracts the X-Csrf-Integrity header from mutating-state requests (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH), base64-decodes it, and calls AWS CloudHSM (cluster ID: cluster-abc123xyz) via PKCS#11 to perform a C_Verify operation using the session-bound ECDSA P-256 key (label: 'csrf-session-key'). The verification checks that the signature covers SHA-256(session_id || request_path || timestamp_window). If C_Verify returns CKR_SIGNATURE_INVALID or the header is missing, the authorizer returns a 403 policy denial before the request reaches the FastAPI Lambda. The CloudHSM key is non-extractable (CKA_EXTRACTABLE=FALSE, CKA_SENSITIVE=TRUE) so the signing key cannot be exfiltrated to forge tokens. The /csrf-token endpoint returns tokens signed with this same HSM key. An attacker on a malicious origin cannot obtain a valid X-Csrf-Integrity header because: (1) the token endpoint requires an authenticated session cookie which is httponly and not readable cross-origin, (2) even if they could read the token via some XSS, the signature binds to the specific request path and 5-minute time window, and (3) CORS policy on API Gateway restricts Access-Control-Allow-Origin to 'https://app.internal.example.com' with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: false for all other origins.

config.api_gateway: AWS API Gateway HTTP API with Lambda authorizer
config.lambda_authorizer: Validates X-Csrf-Integrity header via CloudHSM C_Verify for all state-mutating methods
config.hsm: AWS CloudHSM cluster-abc123xyz, ECDSA P-256 key label 'csrf-session-key', CKA_EXTRACTABLE=FALSE
config.cors_policy: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.internal.example.com only, credentials not allowed cross-origin
